title.narrative: Protect the Life and Livelihood of Affected People in Dollo Ado, Raso and Dollobay Woredas of Liben and Afder Zones, Somali Region (Prolife)

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe project will be implemented by CISP, CUAMM, Wa-PYDO (a local NGO) in Dollo Ado, Raso Dollo Bay woredas of Liben Afder Zones, Somali Region. CISP, as the lead agency, will oversee the project provide technical support to local partner. The consortium has a long-standing presence in the area, extensive partnerships, and significant experience in their respective sectors. CUAMM will focus on Health Nutrition, while Wa-PYDO will handle Agriculture and WASH in Dollo Ado. CISP will implement Agriculture and WASH in Dollo Bay and Raso alongside coordination capacity-building activities. These organizations have previously collaborated on long-term recovery projects in similar sectors, aiming to consolidate those efforts.ltbrgtThe targeted woredas have faced multiple natural and human-made hazards, including drought, conflict, floods, disease outbreaks. Over the past three years, severe drought has resulted in the death of over 1.2 million livestock (2021-2023). In 2023, intensified Gu rains caused significant displacement and destruction of livelihoods. The floods displaced 2,416 people, resulted in 2,121 livestock deaths, and washed away 7,454 hectares of farmland in Dollo Ado and Dollo Bay. The community is now expected to face further severe drought, threatening lives and livelihoods that have yet to recover from previous disasters.ltbrgtGiven the forecasted below-normal rainfall, adverse impacts on agricultural production, water, livestock, and health and nutrition are anticipated. The project proposes anticipatory actions to minimize drought impacts through integrated multi-sectoral interventions: 32% for agriculture, 28% for WASH, 20% for Nutrition, 20% for Health. Agricultural activities include improving animal feed availability, health services, income-generating activities, and conditional cash assistance to support cases of SAM and MAM. The WASH sector will focus on developing groundwater rainwater harvesting systems for both human and livestock, along with promoting hygiene and sanitation practices. The health and nutrition sectors will deliver essential services through a Mobile Health and Nutrition Team (MHNT) across both districts and strengthen the existing health system by providing drugs, equipment, and training for healthcare workers. It two sectors expected to directly benefit a total of 38,904 people through various services, including the diagnosis and treatment of sick adult and under five children, nutritional screening and management of acute malnutrition, vaccination and social behavior change communications to increase awareness of the community on proper nutrition, IYCF and health practices. ltbrgtGender issues, AAP, PSEA will be integrated across all sectors. The failures of five consecutive rainy seasons (2021-2023), combined with drought, cholera outbreaks, and conflicts, have drastically impacted livelihoods and community resilience. This project aims to enhance communities' preventive capacity against the predicted drought.ltbrgtThe overall objective is to support the vulnerable population, enabling them to withstand the anticipated drought through multi-sectoral interventions that protect livelihoods, improve access to basic services, prevent a nutrition crisis. Activities will address the needs of 5,265 IDPs, 3,510 returnees, 26,325 non-displaced affected individuals in Dollo Bay Dollo Ado. CISP its partners will assess ongoing interventions by other agencies to create synergy, avoid duplication, and enhance complementarity.ltbrgtTo achieve the intended results, the project includes need-based activities, a tailored participatory monitoring mechanism, inter-sectoral integration gender-sensitive approaches. Particularly, the project will coordinate closely with local authorities coordination structures including sectoral cluster in all levels. One strategy involves cash-based interventions based on feasibility analyses. The project is budgeted at $575,967.73 for implementation over six months. ltbrgtlt/pgt
